The image is a microscopic view showing:
- A large, round, dark brown-to-black **sporangium** (spore-bearing structure) on the right
- A collapsed, empty sporangium wall/sac (translucent, crumpled remnant) attached to the left
- A sporangiophore (thin filamentous stalk) extending upward-left

This microscopic morphology — large globose dark sporangia on sporangiophores, with characteristic collapsed/emptied sporangial sacs — is diagnostic of **Rhizopus** species. The black sporangia filled with dark spores, and the empty collapsed sporangiophore remnants are textbook features of Rhizopus. The knowledge base specifically describes Rhizopus_Soft_Rots as having "whitish-gray mycelia with **black sporangia**," which aligns directly with this microscope image showing the round, dark brown-black sporangium.
